pair.title: Log in to Withings
pair.instructions: A Withings login window will open. Grant access to your sleep events, then return here.

settings.intro: Optional. Leave blank to use the app's built-in credentials. Fill these in only if you want to use your own Withings application, from the Withings Partner Hub (Public API integration) and tools.developer.homey.app/webhooks.
settings.saved: Saved. Restart the app or re-add the device to apply.
settings.guide_title: How to set up your own Withings application
settings.guide_desktop: Do this on a computer. Open Homey's developer tools, pick the app and go to App Settings — the same fields as here, but far easier to paste into:
settings.guide_step1_body: Choose "Public API integration" as the type. Name it whatever you like. The Client ID and Secret appear on the overview page afterwards.
settings.guide_step1_urls: Register both of these as Registered URLs:
settings.guide_step1_slash: The trailing slash on the callback URL matters. Withings compares character by character, and login fails without it.
settings.guide_step1_base: Register the webhook URL without a query. Each Homey subscribes with its own id appended as ?homey=…, and the base URL covers them all. If a subscription is ever rejected as an unregistered URL, add the full form with your own Homey id as well.
settings.guide_step2_body: Create a new webhook and pick "Query Parameter" as the matching strategy. Copy the ID and Secret from there. Without a webhook the app still works, but polls instead of receiving events instantly.
settings.guide_step3_body: Fill in the four fields above, press Save, then Test connection. The test asks Withings for a nonce, the same call the app makes when refreshing a token — if it succeeds, the ID and secret are right.
